post.description:
Compile PTX to a cubin.

Note this returns HTTP 200 even when the compile *fails*. A failed compile is
a normal, expected answer to a valid question — the caller submitted PTX and
we are telling them what ptxas said about it. A 4xx/5xx would mean the
*request* was wrong, which is a different thing. Distinguish on `ok`.

Compile if needed, then launch on the GPU and return the outputs.

Imported lazily so the compile half keeps working on a machine with no GPU
and no cupy.

RunRequest.title: RunRequest
RunRequest.description:
The launch descriptor.

This is the part that surprises people: a compiled cubin is inert. The PTX
says what one thread does; it does NOT say how many threads to start, how
they're grouped, how much scratch memory they share, or which argument is an
output. All of that has to be supplied at launch, which is why this request
is so much bigger than /compile's.

interpretation: Repeated buffers, 8 warmups and 75 timed iterations, unlocked clocks, no eviction control
64 MiB effective bandwidth exceeds advertised DRAM throughput; cache effects invalidate cold DRAM models for cache-resident repeated workloads
224 MiB input exceeds twice published 96 MiB L2, but no memory counters prove actual DRAM bytes or cold cache state
Published 104.8 TFLOP/s peak assumes GPU Boost clock; conditional arithmetic model is not a rigorous bound for unknown clocks
Grid ceiling scales peak by min(CTA count,170)/170 since each CTA resides on one SM; ignores additional warp/issue/shared-memory constraints
No-work launch median is a timing reference, not an additive cost or universal minimum
Matmul self-comparison uses identical compiler hashes; group ratios reflect noise, not a candidate speedup
Full output checks on first calibration trial, prefixes later; random-input exact float32 strided sum reference
No hosted counters, roofline utilization proof, clock locking or fresh-input-every-iteration claim
